gaps.lead: The show was so dull that half the audience left.
gaps.sentence: It was ___ that half the audience left.
gaps.explanation: so dull (a show) → such a dull show.

gaps.lead: He spoke so quickly that nobody understood him.
gaps.sentence: He spoke ___ for anybody to understand him.
gaps.explanation: so quickly that nobody understood = too quickly (for anybody) to understand.

gaps.lead: She prefers reading to watching television.
gaps.explanation: prefer X to Y = would rather do X than do Y.

gaps.lead: Only after reading the letter twice did it make sense.
gaps.sentence: The letter ___ sense until he had read it twice.
gaps.explanation: It didn't make sense until… = it made sense only after…

gaps.lead: When I was a boy, we walked everywhere.
gaps.sentence: When I was a boy, we ___ everywhere.
gaps.explanation: used to + infinitive expresses a past habit.

gaps.lead: She'll be at work, so she won't answer the door.
gaps.sentence: She'll be at work, so ___ answer the door.
gaps.explanation: won't be able to = future inability.
